data_note: All data is synthetic: generated scenarios with planted labels.
benchmark_caveats: What the robustness seeds test. Ring sizes, evasion rate (20-60%), decoy group sizes, background trade volume and device-sharing noise were varied. The attack types were not: the same three scenarios and the same three decoy kinds appear in every seed. The result is stability to those parameters, not to a new manipulation tactic or a new kind of innocent behaviour.

Robustness result. At the frozen threshold 43.0, precision over the eight seeds was 100% / 100% / 100% and recall 95% / 98% / 100% (min / median / max); worst case seed 101, F1 98%. Every one of the 5 missed attackers scored below the threshold but inside the review band (5 of 5): 2 coordinated_accumulation, 3 mule_funding.

The margin is thin where it matters. Across the robustness seeds the weakest attacker scored 36.79-45.55 and the strongest non-attacker 26.53-41.97 against a threshold of 43.0. On robustness seeds [105, 107] the strongest non-attacker outscored the weakest attacker, so no single cut-off separates them perfectly; the frozen threshold happens to flag no decoy, but it is a few points from the strongest non-attackers and misses attackers in the same range.

Weights and threshold. Weights were set a priori and never fitted. Only the threshold was chosen from data, from the validation seeds. Seed 42 and the robustness seeds were not used for tuning; the validation seeds' 100% F1 is in-sample for the threshold.

Review band. The margin is the mean validation gap, and that gap is dominated by two easy seeds (gaps 16.8, 15.0, 2.3). It is a heuristic for routing cases to the agents, not a calibrated probability. It also routes decoys: see the decoy column of the band table.

Hints. Rewritten after the seed 42 confusion was known, so seed 42 is not held out for it. All attacker alerts on the other seeds were hinted correctly, but the hint is a three-way decision list built for these three scenarios; a new pattern would be hinted as one of them or unclassified. A needs_review alert made only of decoys has no correct hint by construction.

Ablation. Graph features alone reach robustness F1 89% / 97% / 100% (precision stays 100%); behavior features alone 72% / 81% / 93%; device/funding components only 50% / 71% / 92%; the flat funding rule 43% / 62% / 74%; the full detector 98% / 99% / 100%. Graph structure carries most of the separation and behavior adds the last recall points; neither half is as good alone. The graph/behavior split of features is a judgement made before the runs, and the full-detector row's validation F1 is in-sample.
The flat rule scores the same on the original seeds because decoys and evasions are generated identically there; only the background trades differ.

agent_caveats: Decoy and borderline cases are injected needs_review alerts built at the accounts' real detector scores (the decoys score far below the review band), so they test the investigation, not the detector. Seed 42 has no detector needs_review alert.

Only the four real alerts were re-run with the final pipeline; the four EV_ cases are from the previous pipeline (before deterministic membership and removed-claim bookkeeping). Their decisions are unaffected by the change in membership but their report text was not kept.

EV_C004, the one attacker that scored in the review band, was cleared by the agent, which also disagreed with the detector's hint. The threshold and decision logic were not changed to catch it. EV_DG3_busy_honest ended uncertain (not escalated).

Latency varies with Vertex: a send-back call once took 37 s, and a single model call took 346 s during a machine suspend (the deadline watchdog now polls the wall clock). The slowest recorded case is 67.4 s.

limits.title: Results moved between runs: decoys escalated on the re-run
limits.text: The evaluation run (2026-10-16) cleared two decoy groups, left the busy-but-honest one uncertain and cleared the borderline attacker EV_C004. A re-run of the four injected cases on the final pipeline (2026-10-17, one run each) cleared only the household group and escalated EV_C004, the exchange cluster and the busy-but-honest group: 2 of 3 innocent groups falsely escalated (18 accounts, 6 of them added from the ring subgraph). The 0-of-23 false-escalation figure in the agent table is the earlier run's and does not hold for the re-run. Nothing was tuned. See docs/injected-rerun.md.

limits.title: The needs-analyst lane is empty
limits.text: The earlier uncertain result for the busy-but-honest group was not reproduced, so after the re-run no stored case is in the needs-analyst lane (7 escalated, 1 agent-cleared).

limits.title: Recall at ring level follows from escalating whole rings
limits.text: Attacker recall of 39/39 holds because the agent decides for the whole alert and every member of an escalated ring counts. It no longer measures per-account judgement, and the exclusion path was never exercised on this data.

limits.title: The data is synthetic
limits.text: Scenarios, decoys, generator and detector come from one project. The labels say what the generator planted, not what a real market contains. Nothing here is evidence about real prediction markets.

limits.title: Decoy and borderline cases are injected
limits.text: The four EV_ cases are needs_review alerts built at the accounts' real scores, so they test the investigation, not the detector. Seed 42 has no detector needs_review alert, and these four were not re-run after the membership change.

limits.title: The margin is thin
limits.text: One evaded coordination account scored 42.99 against the 43.0 threshold and was missed by the detector. The weights are fixed a priori; only the threshold came from data.
